Frost spreads from this contact across three nearby bronze teeth, changing warm metal into pale blue ice. A short curved motion trace behind the unfrozen upper rim suggests rotation abruptly stopped. Keep the brightest crisp edge where ice wedges against bronze; leave broad quieter stretches elsewhere. Use a few wide opaque strokes within enclosed shapes. Frost is a thin irregular connected crust, not scattered particles or tiny crystal facets.
